covers: Vision acuity/field numbers per eye, blindness criteria, life-sustaining therapy (type 1 diabetes on an insulin pump, times and hours per week).
notes: Re: Disability Tax Credit - supporting medical information
I have followed this patient in my clinic since 2012. They have type 1 diabetes mellitus, diagnosed in 2009,
complicated by proliferative diabetic retinopathy diagnosed in 2016.
VISION
Despite panretinal laser photocoagulation and intravitreal anti-VEGF injections, vision has continued to deteriorate.
Best corrected visual acuity, measured on a Snellen chart at the most recent visit:
Right eye: 20/400
Left eye: 20/200
Visual field: 15 degrees in the right eye and 20 degrees in the left eye.
The patient meets the criteria for blindness in both eyes.
Vision has been impaired to this degree since 2019 and this has lasted more than 12 months.
Vision is not expected to improve.
LIFE-SUSTAINING THERAPY
Type 1 diabetes was diagnosed prior to 2021.
Insulin is delivered by an insulin pump, with continuous glucose monitoring.
Every day the patient checks blood glucose, counts carbohydrates and adjusts insulin doses, at least 4 times per day
(28 times per week).
Time spent on these activities averages 16 hours per week.
This therapy supports a vital function (regulation of blood glucose).
Insulin therapy has been required since 2009 and has lasted more than 12 months. It is lifelong and will not improve.
I have been this patient's physician from 2012 to present. Their medical records are on file in this clinic.
